seo.title: Temperature, Humidity & Light Sensor | Hitelecom
seo.description: Wireless indoor temperature, humidity and light monitoring for museums, archives, galleries and managed spaces. Compare H200 LoRa, H300 4G and H500 NB-IoT.

hero.description: The Hitelecom H Series temperature, humidity and light sensor measures local air temperature, relative humidity and illuminance for indoor monitoring. Designed for museums, galleries, archives and other managed spaces, it connects conditions at selected points with remote review and configured alerts. Custom sensor configurations can be discussed for additional sensing and installation requirements. Choose H200 LoRa, H300 4G or H500 NB-IoT, then match the sensing layout, light measurement and reporting profile to your project.

measurement.description: Room averages tell part of the story. Conditions beside an exhibit, within a display case or near stored materials can differ. A useful monitoring plan identifies both the place being measured and the decision each reading will support.

measurement.installation_text: Mark each monitoring point on a room or case plan. For air measurements, choose exposure that represents the monitored zone and account for nearby vents, doors and heat sources. For illuminance, keep the sensing face unobstructed and record its orientation. Agree reversible mounting for heritage interiors and collection spaces.

workflow.profile_text: Build the monitoring profile around the change you want to see. The measurement interval defines when readings are taken; the reporting interval defines when data reaches the platform. Specify both alongside your alert and battery requirements.

faqHeading.intro: Practical answers for choosing measurement points, collection targets and a wireless monitoring configuration.

faqs.question: What does a temperature, humidity and light sensor measure?
paragraphs: It measures air temperature, relative humidity and illuminance at selected indoor sensing points. Illuminance is expressed in lux and describes the visible light falling on a surface.
Specify the channels, sensing arrangement and measurement performance for the supplied Hitelecom configuration.
faqs.evidence: Direct product channel evidence: official hero image labels Temperature, Humidity and Light. Lux meaning: CCI's illuminance explanation. Image screen values are display examples, never performance limits.

faqs.question: Why monitor temperature, humidity and light together in a museum?
paragraphs: They describe different parts of the environment around a collection. Temperature and humidity observations support climate review; light observations support decisions about display lighting and exposure schedules.
Reading them in the context of the exhibit, its materials and opening hours gives conservators and facilities teams a shared basis for discussion.
faqs.evidence: CCI treats climate and lighting as separate material-dependent preservation factors, and explicitly recommends measuring temperature, RH and light for textile display/storage. Combined page value is an editorial inference from these documented needs.

faqs.question: How should we choose temperature, humidity and light targets for collections?
paragraphs: Start with the collection's materials, their condition, the existing environment and any agreed loan or exhibition requirements. Ask the conservation team to define the targets for each room or case.
Temperature and humidity limits can then inform the alert configuration, while light readings can be compared with the agreed display plan.
faqs.evidence: CCI Climate Guidelines and ClimaSpec select guidance by object type and sensitivity. Hitelecom public page supports configurable temperature/RH thresholds. This is specification guidance, not a universal setpoint recommendation.

faqs.question: Where should sensors be placed in galleries, archives and display cases?
paragraphs: Place the air-sensing point where it represents the collection or zone you want to monitor. Consider shelving height, nearby walls, vents and doors. Treat an enclosed case as its own monitoring location when its internal conditions are important.
Record the point on the site plan and agree the terminal or probe arrangement before installation.
faqs.evidence: NEDCC indexed primary-source text says placement must reflect collection conditions and gives mid-shelf general-monitoring examples. CCI describes spatial gradients and conditions near objects. Probe/mount customization is supported by the manufacturer PDF. Placement wording is project guidance, not a claim of one fixed install height.

faqs.question: Where should the light-sensing face be positioned for an exhibit?
paragraphs: Choose a position and orientation that represent the illuminated surface or display area being assessed. Keep the sensing face clear of shadows from the enclosure, mounts or nearby objects, and record its direction.
Use a commissioning light check at the exhibit to confirm that the fixed monitoring position answers the intended lighting question.
faqs.evidence: CCI defines illuminance as light falling on a surface, recommends measurements for displayed paintings and publishes a tutorial for measuring light on heritage objects. Fixed-sensor orientation and commissioning wording are practical engineering inference from the measurement geometry.

faqs.question: How are lux readings used when reviewing exhibition lighting?
paragraphs: Compare the measured light level with the exhibit's lighting target and note how it changes with daylight, lamp settings and opening hours. Both intensity and duration matter when planning exposure for light-sensitive materials.
If the project requires cumulative exposure analysis, include time-stamped illuminance data, units and the calculation workflow in the platform brief.
faqs.evidence: CCI explains exposure as illuminance multiplied by time; its LED lighting bulletin confirms the continued importance of intensity and duration. Cumulative calculation is framed as a project requirement, not a built-in Hitelecom capability.

faqs.question: How should measurement and reporting intervals be selected?
paragraphs: Choose the measurement interval around the changes you need to observe, such as lighting schedules, case access or room operation. Choose the reporting interval around the team's remote-review and alert needs.
Agree both with the required data coverage and battery plan. A project intended to study brief changes needs a different profile from a long-term seasonal overview.
faqs.evidence: NPS identifies sampling rate as a logger-selection variable and explains its effect on run time/battery. CCI textile guidance supports seasonal monitoring. Reporting distinction is cellular IoT specification guidance; no undocumented minimum interval or continuous streaming is asserted.

faqs.question: Which wireless model and platform should we choose for an indoor installation?
paragraphs: Choose H200 for LoRa, H300 for 4G or H500 for NB-IoT. Evaluate coverage at the actual monitoring points, including enclosed cases, basement stores and internal rooms.

For LoRa, plan the gateway and platform path. For cellular models, confirm local network service and provisioning. Hitelecom Platform or an agreed customer platform can form the monitoring destination.
faqs.evidence: Manufacturer source supports H200/H300/H500, the three wireless options and public/customer cloud deployment. Family-to-radio mapping is confirmed project context. Coverage planning is engineering advice, not a measured range claim.

faqs.question: What measurement performance and calibration information should we specify?
paragraphs: Specify the expected operating conditions and required range, accuracy and resolution for each channel. For light, include the expected low-light or brighter-room conditions and sensing orientation.

Agree how readings will be checked at commissioning, which calibration documents the project needs and a review schedule suited to the installation. Compare the supplied specification with the measurement task.
faqs.evidence: NPS discusses functional range, varying accuracy across range, calibration and periodic checks. Light-measurement geometry comes from CCI. No claim that supplied units include traceable certificates or any fixed recalibration interval.

faqs.question: What should be included when planning battery life?
paragraphs: Use the selected channel list, measurement and reporting intervals, operating conditions and network quality to define the battery plan. Confirm the calculation for the supplied temperature, humidity and light configuration.
The published T&H reference design states more than 10 years at hourly reporting under stated test conditions; that reference should be matched to the final project configuration.
faqs.evidence: Manufacturer reference publishes hourly-reporting battery design; NPS confirms channel/profile/battery relationships. Extension to THL is explicitly a configuration review, not an unverified identical lifetime guarantee.

evidence.factBoundary: Checked on 2026-10-12. FAQ topics are synthesized from traceable public technical practice and product facts. They are not claimed to be collected customer questions, Google/Bing keyword volume, Search Console queries or paid keyword research. Search query links can be reproduced in Google and Bing, but search-engine rank/volume and any first-page result are unverified. The official display image supports the THL channel concept; the existing PDF is a T&H reference. Light range/accuracy/resolution, the final THL protection rating and battery plan are configuration-specific. No UV, PAR/PPFD, automatic lighting control, built-in dew-point/exposure calculation, medical measurement, compliance certification or universal conservation setpoints are asserted.

applications.title: Museum gallery environments
applications.description: Build an environmental record for each gallery rather than relying on one reading for the whole museum. Compare display zones through opening hours, evening shutdown and seasonal changes. Collection-care and facilities teams can review the same local readings when planning room settings or investigating a change.
applications.measurement: Temperature and relative humidity; optional illuminance at selected display positions.
applications.monitoringPoint: Representative display zones, with additional points where layout or room conditions differ.
applications.installation: Use approved wall or freestanding positions with free air exposure and a clear sensing view where light is measured.
applications.projectBrief: Share the gallery plan, collection materials, existing environmental targets and the number of distinct display zones.

applications.title: Enclosed artifact showcases
applications.description: Measure the air inside the case as well as the surrounding room when a collection uses a local microclimate. The two records help staff understand how the enclosure responds to room changes and routine opening. Select a discreet sensing position that works with the case design and object layout.
applications.measurement: Temperature and relative humidity inside the case; optional illuminance where the object is viewed.
applications.monitoringPoint: An approved internal position representing the object compartment, with a separate room reference if required.
applications.installation: Agree the arrangement with the case maker or conservator; maintain seals and keep the device clear of the collection.
applications.projectBrief: Provide case dimensions, compartment layout, buffering or control arrangements and access restrictions.

applications.title: Textile and costume displays
applications.description: Give curators a local record for costumes, tapestries and decorated fabrics during an exhibition. Temperature and relative humidity describe the display climate; an illuminance configuration can help staff check the lighting selected for that textile. Review the readings alongside the display schedule and the conservator's material-specific plan.
applications.measurement: Temperature and relative humidity; optional illuminance for the textile display.
applications.monitoringPoint: Near the displayed material, at a documented light orientation when illuminance is part of the project.
applications.installation: Mount on approved casework or a separate support; preserve viewing space and avoid contact with the textile.
applications.projectBrief: Share textile types, dyes or finishes of concern, display duration, case details and agreed environmental limits.

applications.title: Manuscript and paper display cases

An optional illuminance record helps staff review lighting changes with the exhibition timetable, while temperature and humidity support the local conservation record.
applications.measurement: Temperature and relative humidity; optional illuminance at the displayed paper plane.
applications.monitoringPoint: A case position near the displayed sheet, with the light sensor aligned to the chosen measurement plane.
applications.installation: Use an independent support agreed with the conservator; keep sensing openings clear and allow safe case access.
applications.projectBrief: Provide paper and media types, object plane, lighting layout, exhibit dates and conservation requirements.

applications.title: Natural history specimen displays

Mounted animals, dried plants and minerals can have different environmental priorities, even within one gallery. Local readings give collection staff a basis for reviewing the display arrangement; optional illuminance is useful where the selected specimens are light sensitive.
applications.measurement: Temperature and relative humidity; optional illuminance for selected light-sensitive specimens.
applications.monitoringPoint: The specimen compartment or nearby display air, selected by the collection-care team.
applications.installation: Install on approved exhibition furniture without attaching to specimens or interfering with access and inspection.
applications.projectBrief: Identify specimen materials, enclosure design, preservation methods and which displays require light monitoring.

applications.measurement: Temperature and relative humidity; optional illuminance at selected window-facing objects.

The facility team selects representative room positions and considers the readings alongside occupancy schedules and the building's wider indoor-environment assessment.
applications.measurement: Temperature and relative humidity; optional illuminance at selected learning or daylight positions.
applications.monitoringPoint: Representative occupied room zones and a documented measurement plane for any task-lighting study.
applications.installation: Mount securely clear of occupants and teaching equipment, with air exposure and light orientation matched to the observation goal.
applications.projectBrief: Provide room layouts, teaching schedules, existing concerns, daylight arrangements and the intended monitoring period.

applications.monitoringPoint: Representative collection shelves and reading zones, with extra positions for defined daylight questions.

applications.monitoringPoint: Representative visitor-space air and agreed display positions, selected separately when their purposes differ.

applications.monitoringPoint: Representative occupied and collection positions chosen around the building's use and conservation priorities.

applications.title: Indoor plant collections and conservatories
applications.description: Compare the local environment around indoor plant displays and sheltered conservatory areas. Temperature, humidity and optional illuminance can describe differences between selected positions through the day. Horticultural staff interpret the readings against the needs of the plants and their care routine, with the light configuration agreed for the observation objective.
applications.measurement: Temperature and relative humidity; optional illuminance for selected plant-display positions.
applications.monitoringPoint: Representative plant-display air and light positions chosen by the horticultural team.
applications.installation: Keep sensing openings clear of foliage and irrigation spray; confirm suitability for the expected environment and selected light conditions.
applications.projectBrief: Share plant types, indoor layout, daylight or lamp arrangements, watering routine and the intended observation period.
